lead: Fresh fruit, vegetables, salad, herbs, mushrooms and sea vegetables as sold to eat, organised by crop group and species, then named cultivar, then origin (PDO/PGI/GI), club brand or breeder code, with marketing grades attached.

b.v: Extra Class > Class I > Class II
b.w: UNECE and EU marketing standards for fresh fruit and vegetables; the class is printed on the label or crate.
Fixes the growing area and sometimes the cultivar; a label of origin, not a grade.

b.v: cultivar or club brand named > generic
b.w: Flavour, texture and keeping quality follow the cultivar; club (managed) varieties are sold under a trade mark.

b.v: certified organic (EU leaf, USDA Organic, JAS)
b.w: Official organic schemes set the growing rules.

depts.note: Variety by cultivar. Japanese premium gift fruit (melons, grapes, mangoes, strawberries sold by shops such as Sembikiya and Takano) appears as archetypes or versions inside each kind, with the shops in the brand register.

b.v: U.S. Extra Fancy > U.S. Fancy > U.S. No. 1 (apples, pears); U.S. No. 1 > U.S. No. 2 for most fruit
b.w: USDA AMS grade standards for fresh fruit.

b.v: 特秀 (tokushū) > 秀 (shū) > 優 (yū) > 良 (ryō)
b.w: Grades used by Japanese co-operatives and gift-fruit shops for shape, colour and blemish (to verify).

b.v: measured Brix; tree- or vine-ripened > picked green
b.w: Premium fruit is graded and sometimes guaranteed by sugar content measured with optical sensors.

b.v: count per box or size code
b.w: Trade sizing printed on the box; bigger is not always better.

s.brief: Organise each kind as species → cultivar (archetype) → origin/GI, club brand or breeder code (version) → size, colour, grade (detail), originators and reference cultivars first, never alphabetical. Merge cultivar/GI duplicates (a GI of one cultivar is a version of that cultivar; a multi-cultivar GI or regional heritage group is an archetype with maker-free mk). Breeder codes (e.g. CIVM49, IFG Twenty-Two) are the version reference with the trade mark as alias; breeders and club owners go in the brand register; note the plant-variety record so the C3 living-plants register can link it. Apple: originators and world reference cultivars first (Red Delicious, Golden Delicious, Granny Smith, McIntosh, Cox's Orange Pippin, Fuji, Gala, Braeburn, Honeycrisp, Cripps Pink/Pink Lady, Jazz, Envy, Cosmic Crisp, Bramley), then heritage and regional cultivars, then club varieties with their breeder codes. Japanese premium: Sekai Ichi, Fuji from Aomori/Nagano as versions. Bramley's Seedling with Armagh Bramley PGI as version; Italian, Austrian and Alpine heritage groups (Antiche mele…) and PGIs (Mela Alto Adige, Val di Non) as versions or maker-free archetypes. Brand register: Pink Lady/APAL, Jazz (T&G Global), Envy, Rubens, Kanzi, SweeTango, Cosmic Crisp (WSU). Add a tradition for English apple heritage/orchards if a source supports it. Cut the remaining list to cultivars a reader would meet.
